title: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (GS) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
author: Zacks.Com
description: Goldman Sachs is attracting investor attention with strong earnings growth expectations of +38.1% for the current fiscal year and revenue growth of +25.9%. However, the stock has underperformed the broader market over the past month, declining 6.8% compared to the S&P 500's +0.7% gain. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and a C valuation grade indicating fair pricing relative to peers, the stock is expected to perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

The neutral sentiment reflects balanced positive fundamentals offset by recent underperformance and market-level expectations.

title: Goldman Sachs Is Paying Up to $2.25 Billion for a $30 Billion ETF Business. Is That Enough to Lift the Stock Back to a Record by 2028?
author: Todd Shriber
description: Goldman Sachs announced an acquisition of NEOS Investments for $2.25 billion, adding a $30 billion (now $36.5 billion) ETF business specializing in covered call and options income strategies. While the deal is strategically sound and positions Goldman well in the growing alternative income ETF space, analysts believe it alone won't be sufficient to drive the stock back to its all-time high of $1,146.65, requiring a 30% rally from current levels.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The acquisition is described as 'smart' and 'shrewd,' demonstrating strategic positioning in growing ETF markets. However, the article emphasizes that this deal alone is insufficient to drive the stock back to all-time highs, requiring additional catalysts. The company's core business (investment banking and trading) remains the primary revenue driver, limiting the impact of this bolt-on acquisition.

title: Warren Buffett Has 1 Rule for Investing During Volatility, and It's More Important Than Ever Right Now
author: Ben Gran
description: Warren Buffett's famous investing strategy of being 'greedy when others are fearful' encourages investors to buy stocks during market downturns when prices are discounted. The article explains how average investors can apply this principle by deploying extra cash during bear markets and maintaining consistent long-term investments, demonstrating how $500 monthly investments in index funds could grow to $18 million over 60 years.

title: Former Goldman Sachs Partner Richard Campbell-Breeden Joins SEDA, Expanding Its M&A, PE & Corporate Finance Practice
author: Not Specified
description: SEDA Experts LLC announced that Richard Campbell-Breeden, a former Goldman Sachs partner with 37 years of investment banking experience, has joined as Managing Director. Campbell-Breeden will expand the firm's M&A, private equity, and corporate finance capabilities, bringing expertise in mergers and acquisitions, valuation, corporate governance, and strategic advisory services.

title: Bank of America vs. Goldman Sachs: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Erin Kennedy
description: The article compares Bank of America and Goldman Sachs as investment options for 2026. Bank of America offers stability through its massive consumer banking network and steady cash flow but faces regulatory headwinds and underperformance versus the S&P 500. Goldman Sachs, while navigating a strategic pivot away from consumer businesses, has outperformed the market and the S&P 500 but carries higher leverage and market sensitivity. The author suggests Goldman Sachs may be the better growth investment despite its higher valuation.
